correctness.rationale: For the normalized Glauber generator, translation invariance closes the two-spin hierarchy. Differentiating gives a positive killed random-walk semigroup with uniform initial derivative; the image Bessel kernel telescopes to a finite positive sum S_n. Integrating from the proven Gibbs limit q^n gives the exact monotone C_n(t). Fixed-order Bessel asymptotics and exponential-tail integration give C_n(t)-q^n ~ n exp[-2(1-gamma)t]/sqrt(pi gamma t). Exact exponential-age change of variables then yields the lower-edge probability and density including the logarithmic exponent, with limiting cases treated separately. The stationary pair recurrence gives the unique bounded mean profile, independently checked against six- and eight-spin reset generators. The supplied checker passed 231 deterministic assertions. This is an analytic proof, not extrapolation from finite numerics.

originality.rationale: The principal closely related 2020 study solves a different observable: the thermal/spatial magnetization distribution, and explicitly proposes study of two-point-correlation distributions as further work. The 2024 extension studies a two-dimensional Metropolis-critical magnetization process and does not cover the one-dimensional Glauber pair distribution. The claimed doubled threshold, critical square-root logarithmic divergence and fixed-distance full law do not follow as stated from either article; they require the two-point killed-semigroup spectral edge and a nonlinear renewal pushforward. Targeted search found no equivalent claimed theorem. The underlying Glauber hierarchy, Bessel kernel and renewal mechanism are classical and not claimed as new. Generic resolvent and spectral-edge theorems might imply the present specialization, and full global priority is not certified.

value.rationale: The source 2020 paper identifies two-point-correlation distributions as an open direction. The present theorem solves that natural observable for every fixed spin separation and provides an exact continuous law, a physically distinct reset-rate crossover at twice the magnetization threshold, and a nontrivial logarithmic divergence at the critical rate. The logarithmic factor exposes the relaxation spectral edge and disappears exactly at the zero-coupling boundary. The accompanying explicit stationary spatial profile diagnoses common-clock-induced long-range connected correlations. These are structural results about physically meaningful energy/spin-pair observables rather than arbitrary numerical slices or a simple reparametrization.
